newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cult guru clashes with judge in subway trial.
newsitem.headline: Japan cult guru clashes with judge in subway trial.

text.p: A day after being evicted from his own trial, the cult guru accused of the deadly Tokyo subway gas attack clashed again on Friday with the presiding judge, this time over a glass of water.

In a series of outbursts on Thursday, which led to Judge Fumihiro Abe ordering him to be taken from the court, Shoko Asahara had described the trial as "ridiculous", said he was hallucinating, and sarcastically asked to be sent to the gallows.
On Friday, the leader of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) was back in court and on his best behaviour until about 30 minutes before the end of the morning session.
After sitting quietly for about 90 minutes, Asahara asked a defence lawyer for a glass of water because he was thirsty.
Hearing the request, a prosecution lawyer poured Asahara the water from a jug on a nearby table and handed it to him.
Asahara did not acknowledge the gesture and ignored the glass of water placed on the table in front of him.
Judge Abe told the defendant to drink the water several times before finally warning him: "If you want to drink water, drink it now or we'll take it away from you."
Asahara did not acknowledge the judge's comments, at which point Abe decided to adjourn the morning session 30 minutes early.

Asahara is on trial for the sarin nerve gas attack on Tokyo's subway system in March last year, which killed 12 people and made thousands ill. The cult leader, who has not entered a plea in the case, faces death by hanging if found guilty.
An earlier court appearance by Asahara on October 18 also ended in uproar when he started shaking uncontrollably and asked Judge Abe to jump up and down in his seat.
He spent several days in a padded cell because of worries he would harm himself before doctors determined he could return to his normal cell.
In Friday's testimony, Yoshihiro Inoue, 26, a former chief of the sect's "Intelligence Unit", said that when he first heard of the planned subway attack he did not speak out against it.
"I thought in order to protect the Supreme Truth, it was necessary to kill anything that hinders us," Inoue said.
Police have said the cult launched the nerve gas attack to cause confusion and distract the police ahead of an expected crackdown on the sect.
